neighbours.label: Getting from one place to another: how you travel there or how far/long the trip is. Fires on the mode of travel (by bus, on foot, ride a bike to work, a drive away), on travel time to a place (twenty minutes from the centre), and on the converted figure of a distance between places (e.g. 30 km (19 miles) north of). A bare distance with no travel mode or conversion is weaker (about 0.2). Quiet for measurements that are not trips (weight, width, depth, cooking times) and for 'distance' or 'way' used figuratively.
fire: Most days she takes the bus to the office, which stops right outside her building.
The village lies 30 km (19 miles) north of the capital along the coast road.
He prefers to ride his bike to work when the weather is dry.
The hotel is only twenty minutes from the centre by tram.
We walked there on foot, cutting across the park to save time.
My parents live just a short drive away, so they visit every Sunday.
The airport is about an hour's journey from the city by train.
The monastery sits 12 miles (19 km) east of the nearest town.
quiet: Most days she reads the paper at the office, which sits right above a bakery.
The package weighs 30 kg (66 pounds) and needs two people to lift.
He prefers to repair his bike in the garage when the weather is dry.
The cake needs twenty minutes in the oven at a moderate heat.
We admired the park from the window, watching the leaves change colour.
My parents keep a short distance from gossip and rarely take sides.
The meeting lasted about an hour and ended with a vote.
The table is 12 inches (30 cm) wide and fits neatly in the corner.

predictions: Blind test written by a label-only second author (blind:claude-opus-5-5). Expect most fire items 0.4+; risk: 'bike' in the repair near miss and 'short distance' in the gossip near miss.
